newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ forecasts assume TWI at 68.0 through period.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ forecasts assume TWI at 68.0 through period.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday that its inflation forecasts assume the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) will remain steady at 68.0 throughout the forecast period.
The bank also assumed 90-day bank bills to remain unchanged at 7.5 percent throughout the period.
"These conditions are broadly unchanged from the desired monetary conditions announced on 17 December 1996 (in the Monetary Policy Statement)," it said.
RB Governor Don Brash said the assumed rate was no "quasi guarantee" of the exchange rate.

The December MPS inflation projections were based on a TWI of 66.5 and 90-day rates of 9.0 percent, but the bank said desired monetary conditions were those consistent with a TWI of 66.5 and 90-days at 8.5 percent.

The bank said on Thursday the conditions announced in the MPS had been updated to take account of subsequent information on the December coalition agreement between the National and New Zealand First parties, and import prices.

The RBNZ said it continued to apply a rough rule of thumb that equated the impact on future inflationary pressures of a 100 basis point movement in interest rates on 90-day bank bills with an offsetting two percentage point movement in the TWI.
It would be broadly comfortable with movements in the key monetary indicators that were broadly consistent with such a trade-off.
The TWI was 69.03 at 7.10 a.m. (1910 gmt) on Thursday morning.
